correctness.rationale: Direct single-cycle edge criterion gives Frobenius weights sqrt(2k). A proved support-intersection lemma bounds the number of product cycles, forcing k+l>=9; parity, concavity and support equality isolate (3,6), and >=3 edges cost at least 6. A 3-cycle merging three 2-cycles attains sqrt6+sqrt12; selection and orientations count 16 in each order. Every permutation moving at most five symbols is handled by cycle-type cases, Euclidean chord lower bounds and parity. The actual standalone checker independently passed orders six and seven.

value.rationale: The Birkhoff graph has unweighted diameter two but its physically natural Euclidean edge metric differs from counting moves; the new threshold locates precisely the first support size where cyclewise geodesic additivity fails, with exact strict distance and enumeration of all paths in an infinite family. This is a motivated structural boundary rather than an arbitrary finite table.
